title: Admin activity provenance and retention workflow
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary:
Capture, preserve, and make queryable all administrative and configuration events (admin actions, RBAC changes, access grants, config toggles) with residency-aware retention and an evidence-preservation backend that makes tampering detectable for compliance reviews. This ticket covers the end-to-end workflow: event schema, signer/proof formation, WORM-backed storage integration (S3 Object Lock / encrypted archival), retention policy enforcement, reporting automation, and retrieval interfaces for compliance teams.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
- All admin actions are captured with metadata: actor id, role, IP, request payload hash, before/after diffs, region tag, and timestamp.
- Events are batched and signed into tamper-evident chunks (hash chain + signature) within 30s of event occurrence.
- Chunks written to an immutable storage tier with retention policy enforcement per-organization residency settings (region, retention_days).
- Automated evidence bundles and summary reports produced for compliance ops on a configurable cadence (daily/weekly) with links to underlying sealed artifacts.
- Retrieval API supports time-bound, actor-bound, and config-key queries; exports must include chain proofs and verification instructions.
- Monitoring: ingestion lag, chunk write failures, verification mismatch rate, and storage quota alerts.

Scope / Out of Scope:
- In scope: admin console actions, API admin endpoints, RBAC changes, private deployment admin events, and the evidence storage + reporting automation.
- Out of scope: non-admin user regular chat/query logs (handled by retention policy project separate ticket), or long-term cold archive migration beyond retention window.

Design notes / Implementation plan:
1) Event model and transport:
   - Extend existing events pipeline to tag "admin_provenance" events with standardized fields (actor_email, actor_id, role, client_ip, request_id, region_residency, payload_hash, before_snapshot_ref, after_snapshot_ref, change_type).
   - Use protobuf schema v2 to ensure compact, typed messages.

2) Local buffering & chunking:
   - Events flow to a local collector service per region. Collector batches events into chronological chunks (size ~5MB or 5-minute interval, whichever first).
   - Each chunk includes a chunk_header with chunk_id, start_ts, end_ts, events_count, residency_tag.

3) Tamper-evidence primitive:
   - Each chunk will be hashed (SHA-256) and appended to a region-level hash chain. The collector will sign the chunk hash with a region signing key stored in KMS (asymmetric signing).
   - Signatures and chain anchors will be stored alongside chunk metadata to allow independent verification.

4) Immutable storage integration:
   - Use S3-compatible object storage with Object Lock (governance mode) or an equivalent WORM-capable backend depending on deployment (hosted vs private). For private customers, provide guidance for using their Object Lock/HSM.
   - Store chunk payloads and a separate metadata envelope (json) that contains chain proofs, signature, and verification helper URL. Envelopes are also stored immutably.

5) Residency & retention enforcement:
   - Retention policies declared at org-level: {region: eu-west-1, retention_days: 3650, legal_hold: optional}. Collector will tag each chunk with residency and route to region-local storage only.
   - A retention manager service (cron) enforces deletion/expiry via allowed APIs; for Object Lock, we programmatically set retention and legal holds. For private deployments where Object Lock is unavailable, we document validated operational procedures and provide a retention-enforcement helper tool.

6) Reporting & evidence automation:
   - Generate daily digest reports per org that summarize admin-actions, top-changed config keys, potential policy violations, and links to chunk artifacts. Reports are signed and stored for audit.
   - Provide a one-click export for compliance teams that packages related chunks, signatures, verification instructions, and a human-readable timeline. Exports are delivered via secure share link (expiring) or SFTP for enterprise.

7) Retrieval & verification API:
   - New endpoints: GET /evidence/chunks?start=&end=&actor=&key= and GET /evidence/verify?chunk_id= that return envelope and verification data.

8) Observability & SLOs:
   - Ingestion latency SLO: 99th percentile chunk anchor < 60s.
   - Write success rate >= 99.9% per region per day.
   - Verification mismatch rate < 0.01%.

9) Security & key management:
   - Use KMS for signing keys; rotation process must be auditable and rotations anchored in the hash chain (i.e., rotation events are recorded as special chain entries).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): implement collector + chunking and local signing in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; enable for org-internal admin actions only. Verify with internal compliance team.
- Phase 2 (beta customers): enable for 3 pilot customers with per-org retention settings and report export.
- Phase 3 (general): enable across hosted customers and provide a private-deployment recipe.

Operational runbooks:
- Recovery from chain mismatch: Mark impacted chunk range as "quarantine" and trigger re-sign attempt. Provide a verification tool for compliance to validate signatures.
- Storage failure: Fallback to cross-region write (subject to residency check) and mark with "fallback" tag. Compliance review required if fallback occurs.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we require cryptographic notarization (third-party timestamping) for regulatory customers? (PRO: stronger non-repudiation; CON: complexity + cost).
- For private deployments without Object Lock, should Redwood host a sealed backup mirror? (legal/customer acceptance needed).
- Chunk size vs latency: larger chunks reduce storage overhead and signatures but increase detection latency. Current compromise: 5MB/5min.

Acceptance tests:
- Simulated admin event flow that produces chunks; automated verification script should validate chain end-to-end and assert immutability metadata exists on object storage.
- Retention policy enforcement test: set retention_days=7 and assert deletion or retention_lock behavior after window.
- Report export test: exported bundle validates against verification tool.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Admin+Provenance+Spec (draft)
- Design diagram: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAdminProvenance
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4892

Acceptance criteria checklist: (to be ticked in PR)
- [ ] Event schema extension merged and backwards-compatible
- [ ] Collector chunking service deployed to two regions
- [ ] KMS signing + chain anchoring implemented and end-to-end verified
- [ ] Immutable storage integration pattern documented and demoed with S3 Object Lock
- [ ] Retention manager enforces per-org retention and legal hold
- [ ] Daily digest generation and export flow implemented
- [ ] Retrieval API implemented and secured behind RBAC

Notes on privacy: ensure payload hashes are used to avoid storing raw sensitive configs; where snapshots are needed for compliance exports, respect org-level data redaction policies.
